headline: Gemini integrates Google Keep & Tasks, fixing chaotic workflows
summary: Google's AI can now read your notes and manage your to-dos, turning manual chores into a self-managing ecosystem. See how.
details: Google's Gemini AI is now capable of integrating with Google Keep and Google Tasks, transforming how users manage their personal and professional lives. By enabling Gemini to access Workspace apps, users can automate the process of organizing ideas and managing to-do lists, effectively bridging the gap between thoughts and actions.

To activate this functionality, users must grant Gemini permission to read content from their Google Workspace apps. This is done through the Gemini Settings menu, where the Google Workspace extension can be enabled. Once activated, Gemini acts as a personal assistant, capable of indexing notes and managing tasks with simple prompts.

The integration allows for powerful interactions. For instance, Gemini can summarize lengthy notes from Google Keep, extract specific details like project phases or client inputs, or even retrieve inventory lists. This saves users significant time previously spent manually sifting through information.

Beyond retrieval, Gemini can also create structured tasks in Google Tasks based on information found in Google Keep. A user can ask Gemini to find a recipe in Keep and create a grocery list in Tasks, specifying ingredients and even excluding certain items, demonstrating a sophisticated understanding of context and user intent.

This seamless connection between note-taking and task management aims to solve the common problem of productivity apps becoming cluttered digital junk drawers. By automating the organization and actioning of information, Gemini helps users maintain a streamlined workflow and reduce the daily burden of manual organization.

headline_marked: Snapchat [[stops rewarding AI-generated Spotlight content]] to favor human creators
headline: Snapchat stops rewarding AI-generated Spotlight content to favor human creators
summary: The social media platform is adjusting its recommendation systems to prioritize videos made by real people, aiming to foster authentic creativity.
details: Snapchat has announced a significant policy change: fully AI-generated videos will no longer be eligible for rewards on its Spotlight feature. This move aims to ensure that the platform remains a space for authentic creativity and original content from human users.

The company stated its recommendation systems will be updated to favor content created by real people, emphasizing the value of personal storytelling and unique perspectives. While AI-generated content won't be rewarded, creators can still utilize Snapchat's AI tools for editing and enhancing their videos.

This decision reflects a growing trend across major tech platforms to combat the rise of low-quality AI-generated content, often referred to as "AI slop." Companies are revising their policies to deprioritize such material and promote human-made content.

Other platforms are also taking steps to address AI content. LinkedIn allows users to report "AI slop," Substack offers tools to identify AI-written newsletters, and YouTube has clarified monetization policies to exclude "inauthentic content."
